title: Profiled compile verdict is selected by an observable certificate state
statement: The registered theory gives five observable cases. (1) A concrete regular tilt-DP saddle closes p_reg=g_reg=d and certifies a finite global in-bin labeling; a singular saddle certifies only the generalized DS11 problem. (2) A nonclosed bracket reports its named interval and does not authorize the word optimal. (3) The projected full-efficient-score interval rule remains the currently established unconditional compiler for the distinct projected problem with nuisance information supplied externally. (4) A profiled DS14 companion rule is theorem-backed only along sequences satisfying every audited DS14 law, stability, mass, conditioning, compactness, and projected-separation hypothesis; one measured floor or finite root is diagnostic only. (5) Otherwise compilation of a profiled terminal is refused. On class (L), DS16/DS17 keep the full-triple ordinary-stable companion branch priced and eventually empty. Off (L), DS18 plus DS19 prove that the beta-zero interval DP is Delta-consistent on one exact law, but this value transfer is deliberately not a compile authorization. Strong tilt duality can fail by order one, and the multivariate outer problem is nonquasiconvex.
assumptions: every bracket reports whether it uses the DS11 pseudo-inverse or ordinary DS9 in-bin comparison domain and whether its exhibited primal state is regular
a finite saddle certificate proves finite globality only; population or held-out claims need their own theorem
the projected-rule and in-bin profiled formulations remain distinct
the DS14 companion path inherits all audited DS14 sequence assumptions; a measured nuisance floor alone never suffices
exact scores and raw score-space origin conventions are preserved

role: deployment decision table; DS19 requires a fresh audit before any library landing
